entry.title: [NEW] GHSA-grfq-r75j-rw9x: MariaDB Connector/J: Server could switch character_set_results away from UTF-8 without the client noticing
entry.content:
MariaDB Connector/J: Server could switch character_set_results away from UTF-8 without the client noticing

Aliases: CVE-2026-119281

Severity: CVSS_V3: CVSS:3.1/AV:N/AC:H/PR:N/UI:N/S:U/C:N/I:H/A:N

Affected:

  • org.mariadb.jdbc:mariadb-java-client — fixed in 3.3.7
  • org.mariadb.jdbc:mariadb-java-client — fixed in 3.4.5
  • org.mariadb.jdbc:mariadb-java-client — fixed in 3.5.11

## Summary MariaDB Connector/J decodes every result as UTF-8 and guards `character_set_client` against a change to another charset, but did not guard `character_set_results`, and relied on the server's global `session_track_system_variables` list to be told about charset changes at all. ## Details The connector learns about session variable changes through session tracking, and closes the connection when `character_set_client` is switched away from UTF-8, so that its UTF-8 decoding stays correct. Two gaps remained: - `character_set_results` was not guarded: a server could switch it to another charset, after which the bytes of every result were decoded as UTF-8 although encoded otherwise. - the list of tracked variables came from the server's global `session_track_system_variables…

entry.title: [NEW] GHSA-fhx5-2xqw-2cgm: MariaDB Connector/J: LOAD DATA LOCAL INFILE file check could be satisfied by text inside quoted identifiers, letting a malicious server read client files
entry.content:
MariaDB Connector/J: LOAD DATA LOCAL INFILE file check could be satisfied by text inside quoted identifiers, letting a malicious server read client files

Aliases: CVE-2026-119210

Severity: CVSS_V3: CVSS:3.1/AV:N/AC:H/PR:N/UI:N/S:U/C:H/I:N/A:N

Affected:

  • org.mariadb.jdbc:mariadb-java-client — fixed in 3.3.7
  • org.mariadb.jdbc:mariadb-java-client — fixed in 3.4.5
  • org.mariadb.jdbc:mariadb-java-client — fixed in 3.5.11

## Summary MariaDB Connector/J checked a server's LOAD DATA LOCAL INFILE file request by searching the text of the command it had sent for `LOAD DATA LOCAL INFILE '<file>'`. The search also matched inside quoted identifiers, string literals and comments, so text returned by the server and re-used in a later query could satisfy it. A rogue or MitM server can read any file the client JVM can read. ## Details When a server answers a command with a LOCAL INFILE request (`0xFB` packet), the connector opens the named file on the client host and streams it to the server, after verifying that the file corresponds to a `LOAD DATA LOCAL INFILE` of the command it sent (`ClientMessage.validateLocalFileName()`). That verification was a regular expression whose prefix accepted any character, so it an…

entry.content:
MariaDB Connector/J: Rogue server can drive large heap allocations from server-declared lengths in OK packets

Aliases: CVE-2026-119276

Severity: CVSS_V3: CVSS:3.1/AV:N/AC:H/PR:N/UI:N/S:U/C:N/I:N/A:H

Affected:

  • org.mariadb.jdbc:mariadb-java-client — fixed in 3.3.7
  • org.mariadb.jdbc:mariadb-java-client — fixed in 3.4.5
  • org.mariadb.jdbc:mariadb-java-client — fixed in 3.5.11

## Summary MariaDB Connector/J sized heap allocations from lengths declared by the server in OK packets before checking that those lengths fit in the packet. A rogue or MitM server can make the client allocate megabytes from a packet of a few bytes. ## Details When `CLIENT_SESSION_TRACK` is negotiated (the default), an OK packet carries an info field followed by session-state blocks, each tracked variable being sent as a length-encoded name and value. `OkPacket.parse()` and `parseWithInfo()` allocated `new byte[len]` for the info field, the variable name and the value with the server-declared `len`, then copied the packet data into it. entry.title: [NEW] GHSA-797x-p4mc-jwpm: MariaDB Connector/J: Length-encoded integers larger than Integer.MAX_VALUE were truncated before being used as lengths
entry.content:
MariaDB Connector/J: Length-encoded integers larger than Integer.MAX_VALUE were truncated before being used as lengths

Aliases: CVE-2026-119279

Severity: CVSS_V3: CVSS:3.1/AV:N/AC:H/PR:N/UI:N/S:U/C:N/I:N/A:H

Affected:

  • org.mariadb.jdbc:mariadb-java-client — fixed in 3.3.7
  • org.mariadb.jdbc:mariadb-java-client — fixed in 3.4.5
  • org.mariadb.jdbc:mariadb-java-client — fixed in 3.5.10

## Summary MariaDB Connector/J narrowed 8-byte length-encoded integers received from the server to `int` without validation. A rogue or MitM server can send a value above `Integer.MAX_VALUE` whose truncation becomes a negative or arbitrary length. ## Details The protocol encodes lengths as length-encoded integers, whose 8-byte form the decoder (`readLength()` and `readIntLengthEncodedNotNull()`) returned as `(int) readLong()`. A value above `Integer.MAX_VALUE` therefore wrapped to a negative or unrelated `int`, used afterwards as a length to size allocations or reads, which ended in `NegativeArraySizeException`, out-of-bounds exceptions or oversized allocations. The fix rejects any length-encoded value that does not fit a non-negative `int` with an explicit error. ## Impact Availabil…

MariaDB Connector/J: XA recover() trusted server-supplied gtrid and bqual lengths

Aliases: CVE-2026-119280

Severity: CVSS_V3: CVSS:3.1/AV:N/AC:H/PR:N/UI:N/S:U/C:N/I:N/A:L

## Summary `XAResource.recover()` in MariaDB Connector/J trusted the `gtrid_length` and `bqual_length` columns returned by `XA RECOVER` to allocate and split each Xid. ## Details `MariaDbPoolConnection` and `MariaDbPoolPinnedConnection` built each `Xid` of the recovery list by allocating `new byte[gtrid_length]` and `new byte[bqual_length]` and copying from the `data` column, without validating the lengths against the XA specification bounds (`Xid.MAXGTRIDSIZE`, `Xid.MAXBQUALSIZE`) or the actual payload. Negative or oversized lengths, or lengths that do not fit the data, ended in large allocations or unchecked exceptions (`NegativeArraySizeException`, `ArrayIndexOutOfBoundsException`) during recovery. The fix validates the lengths before any allocation or copy and reports an invalid ro…

entry.title: [UPDATED] GHSA-gv3v-2cpp-3pmq: Keycloak logs sensitive headers
entry.content:
Keycloak logs sensitive headers

Aliases: CVE-2025-11537

Severity: CVSS_V3: CVSS:3.1/AV:L/AC:L/PR:L/UI:R/S:U/C:H/I:N/A:N

Affected:

  • org.keycloak:keycloak-quarkus-server — fixed in 26.5.6

A flaw was found in Keycloak. When the logging format is configured to a verbose, user-supplied pattern (such as the pre-defined 'long' pattern), sensitive headers including Authorization and Cookie are disclosed to the logs in cleartext. An attacker with read access to the log files can extract these credentials (e.g., bearer tokens, session cookies) and use them to impersonate users, leading to a full account compromise. Patches are available, see: - https://github.com/keycloak/keycloak/releases/tag/26.4.11 - https://github.com/keycloak/keycloak/releases/tag/26.5.6 - https://github.com/keycloak/keycloak/releases/tag/26.6.0

entry.title: [NEW] GHSA-f5p5-6xmx-p252: Keycloak vulnerable to authorization bypass via incorrect uri comparison
entry.content:
Keycloak vulnerable to authorization bypass via incorrect uri comparison

Aliases: BIT-keycloak-2026-9800, CVE-2026-9800

Severity: CVSS_V3: CVSS:3.1/AV:N/AC:L/PR:L/UI:N/S:U/C:H/I:H/A:N

Affected:

  • org.keycloak:keycloak-policy-enforcer — fixed in 26.0.10

### Description A flaw was found in Keycloak Policy Enforcer. This vulnerability allows any authenticated user to bypass all authorization policies, including role, scope, and User-Managed Access (UMA) permission checks. By including the configured access-denied page path within a request URL, either as a path segment or a query parameter, an attacker can gain unauthorized access to protected resources.

entry.title: [NEW] GHSA-v3f7-2p4r-mwfw: Keycloak vulnerable to cross-site scripting (xss) via case-insensitive uri validation bypass
entry.content:
Keycloak vulnerable to cross-site scripting (xss) via case-insensitive uri validation bypass

Aliases: BIT-keycloak-2026-9086, CVE-2026-9086

Severity: CVSS_V3: CVSS:3.1/AV:N/AC:L/PR:L/UI:R/S:U/C:H/I:H/A:N

Affected:

  • org.keycloak:keycloak-services — fixed in 26.6.4

### Description A flaw was found in Keycloak. A remote attacker with administrative privileges, specifically those with `manage-client` permission or access to client registration endpoints, could bypass client Uniform Resource Identifier (URI) validation. This is achieved by registering a malicious client with a specially crafted redirect URI using a case-insensitive `javascript:` or `data:` scheme. This Cross-Site Scripting (XSS) vulnerability allows for arbitrary code execution in the Keycloak origin when a victim clicks the crafted link, such as in the logout flow or the Admin Console.

entry.title: [NEW] GHSA-9jrw-8xf7-xqhq: Keycloak vulnerable to information disclosure through arbitrary filesystem path probing
entry.content:
Keycloak vulnerable to information disclosure through arbitrary filesystem path probing

Aliases: BIT-keycloak-2026-9083, CVE-2026-9083

Severity: CVSS_V3: CVSS:3.1/AV:N/AC:L/PR:H/UI:N/S:U/C:H/I:N/A:N

Affected:

  • org.keycloak:keycloak-services — fixed in 26.6.4

### Description A flaw was found in Keycloak. A realm administrator with the "manage-realm" role can exploit this vulnerability by submitting an arbitrary filesystem path as a keystore parameter when creating a key provider component. This allows the administrator to probe arbitrary filesystem paths, determining which files exist and are readable by the Keycloak process. This information disclosure could be used to identify high-value targets for follow-on attacks.

entry.title: [NEW] GHSA-w3p3-7cjg-vgfw: Keycloak allows unauthorized access to resources via uma permission ticket bypass
entry.content:
Keycloak allows unauthorized access to resources via uma permission ticket bypass

Aliases: BIT-keycloak-2026-9799, CVE-2026-9799

Severity: CVSS_V3: CVSS:3.1/AV:N/AC:L/PR:L/UI:R/S:U/C:L/I:L/A:N

Affected:

  • org.keycloak:keycloak-services — fixed in 26.6.4

### Description A flaw was found in org.keycloak.authorization. An authenticated user with a granted User-Managed Access (UMA) permission ticket for one resource can exploit this by using a specific permission request prefix to bypass per-resource access control. This allows the user to gain unauthorized access to all resources of that type within the same resource server, even if they do not have a ticket for those specific resources. This vulnerability requires the resource server to be configured in PERMISSIVE policy enforcement mode and affects typed resources with ownerManagedAccess enabled, where no explicit policy protects the resource type. The primary consequence is unauthorized information disclosure or modification of resources.

entry.title: [NEW] GHSA-r7rc-c989-86g6: Keycloak: Attacker can re-enable and take over disabled clients via registration access token
entry.content:
Keycloak: Attacker can re-enable and take over disabled clients via registration access token

Aliases: BIT-keycloak-2026-9705, CVE-2026-9705

Severity: CVSS_V3: CVSS:3.1/AV:N/AC:L/PR:N/UI:N/S:U/C:L/I:L/A:N

Affected:

  • org.keycloak:keycloak-services — fixed in 26.6.4

### Description A flaw was found in Keycloak's client registration service. A remote attacker, possessing a previously issued Registration Access Token (RAT), could exploit this vulnerability to re-enable a client that an administrator had explicitly disabled. This bypasses security controls, allowing the attacker to reset the client's secret and potentially regain privileged API access. The primary impact includes unauthorized information disclosure and potential integrity compromise.
